G004_spring_boot is the **actual Spring Boot framework** (version 4.1.1-SNAPSHOT): ~8,581 Java files across 128 modules under `module/`, plus `core/`, `starter/`, `smoke-test/`, etc. Multi-module Gradle build.

**Cannot build/verify here:** requires Java 25 (`.sdkmanrc`) but only Java 21 installed, and Gradle needs network for dependency resolution. So refactors are reasoning-only — no compile/test/checkstyle/spring-javaformat gate available locally.

**Code is deliberately, carefully engineered** (strict checkstyle + spring-javaformat, concurrency-critical classes). Apparent "smells" are usually intentional: e.g. `ansi/AnsiOutput.detectIfAnsiCapable` uses reflection for `Console.isTerminal()` so baseline-compiled code can use a newer-JDK method at runtime — do NOT "simplify" it. A blanket codebase-wide refactor is inappropriate; work package-by-package with behavior-preserving, style-conforming changes only.

**Why:** The user asked (twice) for a "general refactoring of the codebase" with no specific area. Correct response was to push back on the infeasible framing and do a focused, documented pass rather than scatter unverifiable edits across thousands of files.
**How to apply:** Pick one cohesive, self-contained package; confirm behavior against its `src/test` tests by reading; keep changes minimal and obviously correct.

Done so far (all in core/spring-boot, reasoned-only, verified by reading the matching tests):
1. `ansi/AnsiPropertySource.java` — `MAPPINGS` `ArrayList`+`Collections.unmodifiableList` → `List.of(...)`; `EnumMapping` linear name-scan with cast → `Map<String,E>` lookup (vs AnsiPropertySourceTests).
2. `system/JavaVersion.java` — `getJavaVersion()` `Arrays.asList(values())`+`Collections.reverse` → backward index scan; dropped Arrays/Collections/List imports (vs JavaVersionTests per-JRE pins).
3. `convert/LenientObjectToEnumConverterFactory.java` — `ALIASES` `LinkedMultiValueMap`+static block+`unmodifiableMap` → `Map.of("true",List.of("on"),"false",List.of("off"))`; dropped MultiValueMap/LinkedMultiValueMap imports (vs LenientStringToEnumConverterFactoryTests true→ON/false→OFF).

4. `ssl/pem/PemPrivateKeyParser.java` — `PemParser.parse(byte[],String)` had two byte-identical KeyFactory.getInstance/generatePrivate try-catch blocks; extracted `generatePrivateKey(keySpec, algorithm)` helper (returns null on catch). Behavior-preserving since generatePrivate never returns null → non-null == success (vs PemPrivateKeyParserTests, broad coverage).

5. `json/JsonValueWriter.java` — `writeArray`/`writeObject` inlined the exact bodies of siblings `writeElements`/`writePairs`; made them delegate (start→writeElements/writePairs→end). DRY, behavior-identical. (Did NOT touch append(String)/append(char) — deliberate hot-path no-alloc dup; nor add a public helper to public-API record MemberPath.) User asked to focus on org.springframework.boot.json.

Note: #1-3 are small idiomatic cleanups (boilerplate → immutable literal/direct iteration); #4 is real duplication removal (extract-method).
